encounters.cc: Worsening headaches, fatigue, and muscle weakness despite adherence to antihypertensive regimen.

lines: Worsening headaches, fatigue, and muscle weakness despite adherence to antihypertensive regimen.
She presents to the clinic with a 6-month history of worsening headaches, fatigue, and muscle weakness.
She also reports experiencing episodes of palpitations and diaphoresis.
Her past medical history is significant for hypertension, which was diagnosed 2 years ago and has been poorly controlled despite compliance with a three-drug regimen.
She takes amlodipine, lisinopril, and hydrochlorothiazide.
The patient expresses a strong preference for non-surgical management due to a fear of surgery.
An abdominal CT scan shows a 2 cm mass in the left adrenal gland with no evidence of bilateral adrenal hyperplasia.

encounters.cc: Uncomfortable creeping sensation in legs, particularly in the evenings and at night, with urge to move.

lines: Uncomfortable creeping sensation in legs, particularly in the evenings and at night, with urge to move.
The patient is a 52-year-old female with type 2 diabetes, hypertension, hypothyroidism, and PUD who returns following her recent endocrinology evaluation for hyperaldosteronism.
She describes it as a deep-seated urge to move her legs, accompanied by a creeping, crawling feeling.
These symptoms have been progressively worsening over the past six months and are temporarily relieved by walking or stretching.
She denies any pain, weakness, or sensory changes in her legs.
She denies smoking, alcohol, or illicit drug use.
On physical examination, her vital signs are within normal limits, and neurological examination shows no abnormalities.

encounters.cc: Progressive left shoulder pain and stiffness with difficulty reaching overhead and behind back.

lines: Progressive left shoulder pain and stiffness with difficulty reaching overhead and behind back.

The patient is a 52-year-old female with Type 2 diabetes, hypertension, hypothyroidism, and peptic ulcer disease, evaluated for primary hyperaldosteronism and restless legs syndrome, who presents with a 6-month history of progressive left shoulder pain and stiffness.
She reports difficulty in reaching overhead and behind her back and denies any recent trauma or injury to the shoulder.
She has a past medical history of type 2 diabetes mellitus and hypothyroidism, which are well-controlled with metformin and levothyroxine, respectively.
Smoking: Never. Alcohol: None. Occupation: Administrative Assistant.
On physical examination, there is a noticeable decrease in both active and passive range of motion of the left shoulder in all directions.
There is no erythema, warmth, or swelling.
The rest of the musculoskeletal examination is unremarkable.

encounters.cc: Chronic dull lower back pain for 6 months that worsens with movement and at the end of the day.

lines: Chronic dull lower back pain for 6 months that worsens with movement and at the end of the day.
The patient is a 53-year-old female with type 2 diabetes mellitus, hypertension, hypothyroidism, peptic ulcer disease, and adhesive capsulitis who presents for evaluation of chronic lower back pain.
She describes the pain as a constant dull ache that worsens with movement and at the end of the day.
She has tried over-the-counter acetaminophen and ibuprofen with minimal relief.
She expresses interest in exploring complementary and alternative medicine (CAM) options, as she is concerned about the side effects of conventional medications.
She inquires about the use of acupuncture and herbal supplements.
Her medical history is significant for a remote history of peptic ulcer disease.
She is currently taking metformin and lisinopril.
Smoking: Never. Alcohol: None. Occupation: Administrative Assistant.
On physical examination, there is tenderness to palpation over the lumbar paraspinal muscles without neurological deficits.
- Liver function tests: Within normal limits

encounters.cc: Intermittent, severe, sharp electric shock-like pain on the right side of her face triggered by chewing.

lines: Intermittent, severe, sharp electric shock-like pain on the right side of her face triggered by chewing.
The patient with Type 2 diabetes mellitus, hypertension, hypothyroidism, peptic ulcer disease, and prior restless legs syndrome presents to Neurology.
She reports a 6-month history of intermittent, severe, sharp pain on the right side of her face.
The pain is triggered by chewing and sometimes by touching her face.
She describes the pain as "electric shocks" lasting for a few seconds to two minutes.
Her medical history is significant for hypertension, controlled with hydrochlorothiazide, and type 2 diabetes mellitus, managed with metformin.
Smoking: Never. Alcohol: None. Occupation: Administrative Assistant.
On physical examination, there is no facial asymmetry or sensory loss, but she winces when the right cheek is lightly palpated.

encounters.cc: Persistent headaches for 6 months with recent onset of right-sided weakness and worsening with coughing.

lines: Persistent headaches for 6 months with recent onset of right-sided weakness and worsening with coughing.
The 55-year-old with diabetes and hypertension returns to neurology with headaches, having presented for restless legs and neuralgia.
She describes constant, dull headaches worsening with coughing and bending over, denying nausea, vomiting, or changes in vision.
Her medical history is significant for hypertension, well-controlled on hydrochlorothiazide.
Smoking: Never. Alcohol: None. Occupation: Administrative Assistant.
On physical examination, she has a mild right-sided hemiparesis and a positive right Babinski sign.
MRI of the brain with contrast shows an extra-axial, dural-based mass lesion with a homogenous enhancement pattern, located at the convexity of the left parietal lobe.

encounters.cc: 6-week history of progressive left breast redness, swelling, warmth, and persistent itching.

lines: 6-week history of progressive left breast redness, swelling, warmth, and persistent itching.
The patient with Type 2 diabetes, hypertension, hypothyroidism, peptic ulcer disease, and meningioma presents with breast complaints.
She reports that the breast has become red, swollen, and warm to the touch.
She denies any trauma or insect bites but notes a persistent itching sensation.
She has not had any fever, chills, or weight loss.
Her past medical history is significant for hypertension, controlled with hydrochlorothiazide.
Smoking: Never. Alcohol: None. Occupation: Administrative Assistant.
On physical examination, the left breast appears erythematous and edematous with a peau d'orange appearance.
There is no nipple discharge, but palpation reveals a firm, irregular mass in the upper outer quadrant and palpable left axillary lymph nodes.
Mammography shows skin thickening and an ill-defined mass.
A core needle breast biopsy and full-thickness skin punch biopsy are performed.

encounters.cc: Severe right upper quadrant pain radiating to right shoulder after fatty meal with nausea and vomiting.

lines: Severe right upper quadrant pain radiating to right shoulder after fatty meal with nausea and vomiting.

This 57-year-old female with type 2 diabetes mellitus, hypertension, and recent history of inflammatory breast carcinoma and meningioma presents to the emergency department with a 24-hour history of severe right upper quadrant (RUQ) pain that radiates to her right shoulder.
She reports the pain began after eating a fatty meal and has been constant since onset.
She also complains of nausea and has had one episode of vomiting.
She has a past medical history of hypertension and type 2 diabetes mellitus.
Smoking: Never. Alcohol: None. Occupation: Administrative Assistant.
On examination, her temperature is 38.3°C (101°F), heart rate is 102 beats per minute, and blood pressure is 135/85 mmHg.
RUQ palpation elicits significant tenderness, and Murphy's sign is positive.
An abdominal ultrasound shows gallbladder wall thickening and pericholecystic fluid without evidence of gallstones.
